response_language.description: Language selected semantically for the reply. English is the default for new or uncertain conversations. Preserve the established language for short, mixed, or ambiguous messages; switch only when the customer explicitly requests another language or clearly communicates predominantly in it.

reply_language_consistent.description: True only when the complete natural-language reply is coherent in response_language, apart from proper nouns, URLs, identifiers, code, and other unavoidable literals.

intent.description: The customer's current underlying intent, inferred from the whole conversation rather than keywords.

conversation_phase.description: A concise semantic description of where the conversation currently stands; do not force it into a fixed funnel.

customer_readiness.description: A concise evidence-based assessment of the customer's present readiness to progress or commit.

commercial_readiness.description: Semantic readiness selected by the model from the complete conversation and evidence.

scope_sufficiency.description: Whether known scope is sufficient for the next commercial action without another redundant confirmation.

customer_goal.description: Cumulative customer outcome in semantic terms; empty only when it is genuinely unknown.

delivery_surfaces.description: Where the proposed solution itself operates.

conversation_channels.description: Where end users converse with the assistant.

handoff_destinations.description: Where human operators receive escalated conversations.

required_capabilities.description: Cumulative capabilities confirmed or requested by the customer.

operational_constraints.description: Cumulative constraints, dependencies, assumptions, and material unknowns.

material_blocker.description: The single genuinely material unresolved issue preventing every safe, useful, reversible next step, or an empty string when none exists. Optional onboarding details are not material blockers.

next_best_action.description: The best concrete customer-visible action to perform in this reply. It must create an externally observable outcome, not describe internal note-taking, preparation, planning, or future work. When the customer is ready to proceed and no material blocker remains, it must include one grounded recommendation or value synthesis and one explicit, easy-to-answer commitment request. When scope, amount, currency, terms, and authorization are grounded, execute the eligible commercial action and provide its instructions instead of reopening discovery.

commercial_progress.description: The concrete customer decision, commitment, objection resolution, or support outcome this reply should create. Internal assistant activity, acknowledgment, paraphrase, or a promise to prepare something later is not progress.

decision_status.description: Semantic state of the customer's decision. Explicit acceptance of the immediately preceding proposal counts as agreement; a compatible refinement or optional unresolved detail does not revoke or downgrade it.

confirmed_commitments.description: Cumulative customer-approved decisions and constraints from the conversation. Preserve compatible prior agreements and never reopen unchanged commitments. When a short assent clearly accepts the uniquely pending proposal, record that proposal as confirmed.

pending_customer_commitment.description: At most one genuinely unresolved customer action required to progress. Use null when none remains or when the customer has supplied or accepted it. An optional implementation detail, repeated final confirmation, or internal planning step is neither a pending customer commitment nor a material blocker.

action.description: Canonical conversational action. Must be escalate whenever should_escalate is true, silent only when should_reply is false, and reply otherwise.

should_escalate.description: Set true only when the runtime must persist and dispatch a human handoff. A direct request to stop automation and speak with a human is sufficient. Never claim a handoff in reply while this is false.

escalation_reason.description: Concise operational reason when should_escalate is true; null otherwise.

contact_profile.description: Complete contact-memory assessment for this turn. Use null for unknown scalar values and empty arrays for unknown list values; never guess or invent contact facts.

language.description: Explicitly requested or semantically clear preferred conversation language. Do not infer it from names, locations, phone codes, currencies, quoted text, isolated words, or metadata.

preferred_contact_channel.description: The contact channel explicitly preferred by the customer, or null when not known.

preferred_contact_time.description: The customer-provided preferred follow-up time or time window, or null when not known.

timezone.description: The customer-provided or reliably inferred timezone for follow-up, or null when not known.

action_id.description: ID of an enabled external side-effect action from the authoritative commercial catalog. Never use a dialogue-stage or planning-artifact ID.

selection_reason.description: Semantic reason this is the nearest useful commercial step, grounded in explicit customer commitments and supplied context.

requested_commitment.description: One concrete customer commitment requested by the selected action; never a repeated or invented prerequisite.

grounding_reference.description: A short literal excerpt from supplied authoritative context that proves either the exact total or that the missing fact is mandatory.

missing_fact.description: Only for request_required_fact: the single genuinely mandatory fact still absent. Null for all other actions.

customer_commitment.description: A short exact excerpt from the newest inbound customer message grounding the selected action. For request_custom_proposal this may express unambiguous commitment to the uniquely active scope and is not payment authorization.

authorization_is_explicit.description: For payment or another external action only: whether the newest inbound message explicitly authorizes that exact action.

authorization_is_unambiguous.description: For payment or another external action only: whether the authorization in the newest inbound message is unambiguous.

authorization_evidence.description: For payment or another external action only: a short exact authorization excerpt from the newest inbound customer message.

authorization_scope.description: The exact grounded active scope for a proposal request, or the exact service, option, amount, and action authorized for an external transaction.

commercial_action.description: A declared durable internal commercial transition or a grounded external side effect. Never use it for ordinary dialogue, discovery, planning, recommendations, or memory updates.

commercial_next_step.description: LLM-selected commercial progression grounded in conversation, memory, RAG, private policy, and verified tool results.

action_required.description: True exactly when the seller-owned next step requires a durable commercial action in this turn.

action_id.description: The matching commercial_action.action_id when action_required is true; otherwise null.

customer_outcome.description: The business outcome the customer is trying to achieve, stated without inventing facts.

recommended_step.description: The single best reversible next step selected semantically by the model.

why_now.description: Why this step is appropriate now, based on current evidence.

customer_commitment.description: The concrete commitment requested from the customer, if any.

seller_commitment.description: The concrete commitment offered by the company, if any.

instructions.description: Grounded operational payment instructions, never a canned response.

active_workstream.description: Concise semantic description of the outcome or service currently being discussed.

workstream_changed.description: True only when the customer materially changed the active outcome or service in this turn.
